messages.content: You are a precise biomedical information extraction assistant. Follow the requested output format exactly and never add explanations.

Given the following text and a relational triplet extracted from it:

Text: Do not inject into a muscle (intramuscularly) or vein (intravenously).
Do not mix insulin and tirzepatide together in the same injection.
You may give an injection of tirzepatide and insulin in the same body area, but not right next to each other.
Your doctor will probably start you on a low dose.
This dose may be gradually increased.
However, it will not be increased more than once every 4 weeks.
You may change the day of the week you use tirzepatide as long as there are at least three days between doses.
Do not stop taking Tirzepatide without talking to your doctor.
Tirzepatide KwikPen:
The KwikPen contains 4 fixed doses.
One dose is injected weekly (subcutaneously).
For your weekly dose, you need to turn the dose knob all the way until KwikPen stops.
You also need to turn the dose knob until the 1 icon is in the dose window.
After 4 doses, throw away (discard) the Pen, including the unused medicine.
The Pen will prevent you from dialing a full dose after you have given yourself 4 weekly doses.
Do not inject the leftover medicine.
Triplet: ["Tirzepatide KwikPen", "has fixed dose", "4 doses"]

The relation 'has fixed dose' in the triplet is defined as 'The subject drug is available in a fixed number of pre-determined doses.' In this context, is there any relation appropriate to replace it? Choose a relation whose meaning and subject/object direction match the triplet even if the wording differs; choose 'None of the above' only if no candidate fits. Please answer by providing only the letter of your choice.

Choices:
A. 'has same doses as': The subject drug is available in the same dose amounts as the object drug.
B. 'has strength': The subject drug is available in the dose strength specified by the object entity.
C. 'has dosage form': The subject drug is available in the pharmaceutical dosage form specified by the object entity.
D. 'has dose increment': The subject drug's dose is increased by the specified amount at regular intervals.
E. 'has recommended dose': The subject drug is typically prescribed at the dose or dosing regimen specified by the object entity.
